item.title: Fijiana ready for biggest physical test against South Africa this Saturday - Legge
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV have turned their attention to winning collisions as preparations intensify for Saturday's Test against South Africa. Head coach Mike Legge says the team's first training session at Buckhurst Park today is primarily about getting the players back on the field after an eight-day break following the Super Rugby Women's season.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV have turned their attention to winning collisions as preparations intensify for Saturday's Test against South Africa.

Head coach Mike Legge says the team's first training session at Buckhurst Park today is primarily about getting the players back on the field after an eight-day break following the Super Rugby Women's season.

Legge says the biggest lesson from Drua Women's Super Rugby Women's final defeat to the NSW Waratahs was the importance of dominating the physical contest.

He says he expects South Africa to present one of the toughest physical challenges the team has faced.

Insert: Legge - South Africa is a big team July 03

Legge says the South Africans arrive in Fiji in good form after a recent Test series against the United States and are continuing to improve.

He says they are in the top 10 for a reason, and will be a physical side that will test them.

While the contact area will be a major focus throughout the week, Legge says the team would remain committed to its attacking style of rugby.

The remaining members of the squad are also expected to join camp as preparations continue for Saturday's Test against South Africa.

The Fijiana's first Test against the Springboks will be held at the HFC Bank Stadium this Saturday at 2pm, while their second Test will be held at Churchill Park in Lautoka next Saturday at 1pm.

item.title: Team Fiji ends Glasgow Commonwealth Games campaign in 20th place
item.description: Team Fiji has finished 20th at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, winning one gold medal through weightlifter Taniela Rainibogi and one bronze medal through boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama. They share the spot with the Bahamas and the Isle of Men.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji has finished 20th at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, winning one gold medal through weightlifter Taniela Rainibogi and one bronze medal through boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama.

They share the spot with the Bahamas and the Isle of Men.

The other standout performer for Team Fiji was swimmer David Tolu Young who finished 6th in the 50 metres freestyle finals.

Young is the first Fijian swimmer to make the finals in swimming.

Meanwhile in last night's competitions, Team Fiji judoka, Gerard Takayawa won his round of 16 elimination match in the Men's +100kg division defeating Adam Hall of Northern Ireland 101-0.

Takayawa went down to Canadian John Bassong in the quarterfinals 100-0.

He also lost out to Gregor Miller of Scotland in the repechage.

Team Fiji Swimming and Basketball athletes were welcomed back by Assistant Minister for Youth and Sports Aliki Bia last night.

Meanwhile, Australia dominated the medal tally with 70 gold, 45 silver, and 56 bronze, England is second with 29 gold, 45 silver, 36 bronze, while Canada scooped third with 19 gold, 20 silver and 23 bronze medals.

item.content:encoded:
It is back to the drawing board as the Ratu Kadavulevu School U18 team prepares for this week's Vodafone Super Deans quarterfinals.

Assistant Coach Jone Ketedromo stated this after they beat Ratu Sukuna Memorial School 43-14 on Saturday, saying that all teams coming up are well prepared especially as it is the National quarterfinals.

Ketedromo says they are not underestimating any team, so they will go back and prepare themselves accordingly on how they can progress to the next round.

Insert: Building on from last year Aug 3

He also thanked all the supporters from the parent, exscholars as well as other stakeholders for keeping their faith in the team.

The Vodafone Super Deans quarterfinals draws have not yet been announced.

item.title: Rewa sharpens finishing ahead of crucial OFC opener against Galaxy FC
item.description: Rewa FC coach Tevita Waranivalu says the team’s preparations for the OFC Men's Champions League have been progressing well, with the side now in the final stages of its build-up ahead of its opening match against Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC this Saturday. Waranivalu saysthe team has been working hard, with the main focus on improving its finishing.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC coach Tevita Waranivalu says the team’s preparations for the OFC Men's Champions League have been progressing well, with the side now in the final stages of its build-up ahead of its opening match against Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC this Saturday.

Waranivalu saysthe team has been working hard, with the main focus on improving its finishing.

Waranivalu says the team has been focusing more on finishing off chances, as Rewa has been a consistent side throughout the league but finishing has been the main concern.

With Rewa set to represent Fiji on home soil, Waranivalu says the expectations are high for the team to perform in front of local supporters.

He says he has reminded the players to remain calm under pressure, adding that representing the country, the club and their families in front of their own crowd is something they should feel proud about.

Rewa FC will face Galaxy FC of Vanuatu this Saturday at 3pm in their opening OFC Men's Champions League match at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

item.title: Fiji needs $300 million to upgrade sporting facilities - Mazey
item.description: Fiji requires an estimated $300 million to upgrade its sporting facilities, according to Fiji Sports Commission Chairman Peter Mazey. He says the country's ageing infrastructure remains one of the biggest challenges facing local sports.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji requires an estimated $300 million to upgrade its sporting facilities, according to Fiji Sports Commission Chairman Peter Mazey.

He says the country's ageing infrastructure remains one of the biggest challenges facing local sports.

Mazey made the comments while responding to concerns raised by Fiji Pearls coach Michelle Parsons about the standard of netball facilities in the country.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Parsons says the difference between the courts in Fiji and Australia became evident during the Fiji Pearls' recent participation in the Spirit Games in Sydney.

She says the players were amazed by the quality of the playing surface in Australia, describing it as vastly superior to what they are accustomed to in Fiji.

Parsons says the court at Vodafone Arena is slippery, making it difficult for players to stop and change direction naturally during matches.

She adds that the poor surface forces players to mechanically adjust their movements, increasing the risk of injury and affecting performance.

Parsons also highlighted that children as young as eight and nine years old in Australia are playing on courts that are of a higher standard than those available to Fiji's national players.

She stressed that Fiji needs significant investment in sporting facilities if athletes are to compete consistently at the highest level.

Mazey acknowledged the concerns, noting that the courts at Vodafone Arena are shared by several sports, making upgrades more complex.

He said infrastructure is a major challenge across all sporting codes and the financial commitment required is substantial.

Mazey says the Sports Commission estimates it needs about $300 million to modernise sporting facilities around the country, comparing the scale of the investment to constructing a new Colonial War Memorial (CWM) Hospital.

He added that, for now, the commission is working with the resources it has while continuing to seek funding for major upgrades.

Meanwhile, Parsons says Fiji also has an opportunity to strengthen its position in international netball if the sport is included in the 2032 Olympic Games.

She noted that greater male participation is one of the requirements being discussed internationally and believes Fiji compares well with many other countries in encouraging men to play the sport.

item.title: Extra Premier League: Rewa thrash Suva 4-0 to build confidence ahead of OFC campaign
item.description: Rewa FC has received a timely boost ahead of their OFC Men's Champions League campaign after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Suva FC in their Extra Premier League Round 16 match at Churchill Park. The Delta Tigers produced a dominant performance, with goals from Josaia Sela, Asivorosi Rabo, Semi Matalau and Neemish Prasad securing all three points for Rewa.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC has received a timely boost ahead of their OFC Men's Champions League campaign after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Suva FC in their Extra Premier League Round 16 match at Churchill Park.

The Delta Tigers produced a dominant performance, with goals from Josaia Sela, Asivorosi Rabo, Semi Matalau and Neemish Prasad securing all three points for Rewa.

Rewa’s strong performance will give the defending champions added confidence as they continue their push in the Extra Premier League.

The win comes at an important time for the Delta Tigers as they prepare to begin their OFC Men's Champions League campaign at Churchill Park next Saturday, where they will meet Vanuatu's Galaxy FC at 3pm.

Meanwhile, Navua FC also recorded a big win in Round 16, defeating Tailevu Naitasiri FC 7-2.

The result strengthens Navua’s position on the points table, while Tailevu Naitasiri’s battle to avoid relegation becomes tougher with only two rounds remaining.

Lautoka FC defeated Nadroga FC 3-1 at Churchill Park.

In yesterday's results, Ba FC defeated Labasa FC 2-1, while Nadi FC beat Nasinu FC 3-2.

item.title: Labasa Sanatan Tournament: Namara Sanatan eyes title in final against Krishna's Emily Sanatan
item.description: Namara Sanatan will face football star Roy Krishna's Emily Sanatan in the 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament final after securing a narrow victory over Lajonia Sanatan in today's semi-final. Namara Sanatan defeated Lajonia Sanatan 1-0 in a hard-fought encounter to book their place in the title decider.
item.content:encoded:
Namara Sanatan will face football star Roy Krishna's Emily Sanatan in the 2026 CK's Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament final after securing a narrow victory over Lajonia Sanatan in today's semi-final.

Namara Sanatan defeated Lajonia Sanatan 1-0 in a hard-fought encounter to book their place in the title decider.

Team captain and current Labasa representative Ashneel Raju says his side is expecting another tough match in the final, adding that playing against a team featuring Krishna will be an exciting and thrilling encounter.

He says it will be a challenging contest, but the team is fully prepared and determined to bring the title home.

Emily Sanatan booked their place in the final after defeating Namolink Sanatan 4-0 in the first semi-final, with Krishna returning to the side after serving a one-match suspension.

The final between Namara Sanatan and Emily Sanatan is expected to kick off at 5.30pm.
